title: SDK/API launch playbook — function calling, structured output, streaming
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Objective: Coordinate the cross-functional launch for SDK updates and API surface changes that enable function calling, structured output, and streaming. This ticket consolidates launch content, release-notes copy, sample matrices, and pre-launch checks to ensure developer-focused onboarding and minimal customer disruption.

Scope:
- SDKs (Python, Node, Go) — surface-level APIs for function calling, typed structured output helpers, and streaming client primitives.
- REST/HTTP API changes and examples for structured output and function metadata.
- Docs: quickstarts, migration guide (backward compatibility), API reference updates, and a new "structured outputs" conceptual guide.
- Samples: small end-to-end apps demonstrating (1) function-calling orchestration, (2) validated structured JSON schemas, (3) streaming token-handling and reconnects.
- Release notes and changelog entries for public web site, SDK changelogs, and email/console in-product banner copy.

Acceptance criteria:
1) SDK PRs merged in main branches with passing CI and integration tests that run against staging API.
2) Docs PRs merged and staged on docs.redwood.ai; quickstarts validated by sample automation.
3) Release notes copy reviewed by PM + Eng + DevRel + Legal; final copy published to release channel.
4) Rollout plan documented with canary percent, rollback trigger metrics, and feature flags.
5) Post-launch monitoring dashboard (Console) configured: errors per 1k calls, median streaming latency, function-calling failure rate.

Rollout plan (high level):
- Week T-2: Branch cut for SDK-beta; internal dogfood samples; DevRel early access.
- Week T-1: Docs and samples publicly staged; cross-team dry run (Eng + SDK + Docs + Support).
- Day 0: Release docs + SDKs + public release notes; enable feature flag at 10% traffic in hosted API; monitor metrics.
- Day 1-3: Increase to 50% if no regression; full enable on Day 7.

Risks and mitigations:
- Compatibility regressions: keep older SDK surface unchanged, provide migration helpers and automated deprecation warnings in logs.
- Streaming regressions causing higher latency: initial canary at low traffic, autoscale dedicated pools if tail latency spikes.
- Security: structured output introduces new parsing surfaces — security review required and completed prior to GA.

Key stakeholders:
- Eng (runtime & API): Priya Shah (ENG-4182 owner), Ben Ortiz (streaming kernels)
- SDK owners: Maya Chen (Python), Jules Park (Node), Omar Khan (Go)
- Docs & DevRel: Elena Martinez (guide + quickstarts), DevRel team for samples and blog post
- Design: Tasha Nguyen (UX samples & code snippets)
- Support & Success: Rajiv Menon (customer comms & FAQ)

Deliverables:
- PRs: SDK repos, api-spec PR (openapi), docs PR, samples repo PRs.
- Release notes: short + expanded versions for email/blog.
- Post-launch checklist and dashboard links.

Notes: Keep the release notes short and developer-centric — show minimal code snippets for each surface and link to full quickstarts. Prioritize stability for Dedicated & Private customers by validating same behavior in VPC staging environments.
